function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to read the output of a command from here, so I can’t tell you directly whether a VPN client is present on this machine.  
However, you can quickly check yourself with a one‑liner that looks for common VPN installers or executables.

**Option 1 – Search the “Uninstall” registry key (PowerShell)**  
```powershell
Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* |
    Select-Object -ExpandProperty DisplayName |
    Where-Object { $_ -match 'VPN' }
```
If anything shows up, you have a VPN client installed.

**Option 2 – Look for a few popular VPN executables**  
```powershell
$paths = @(
    'C:\Program Files\OpenVPN\openvpn.exe',
    'C:\Program Files\Cisco\Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client\vpnui.exe',
    'C:\Program Files\NordVPN\nordvpn.exe',
    'C:\Program Files\ExpressVPN\ExpressVPN.exe'
)
$paths | ForEach-Object {
    if (Test-Path $_) { Write-Output "$_ is installed" }
}
```

Run either of those in a PowerShell window (or copy the command into a `.ps1` file and execute it).  
If nothing appears, it’s likely that no VPN client is installed on this system.
